occupational_task: Confer with company officials about financial and regulatory matters.
basis: Within this audit-heavy source cluster, conferring with officials supplies and communicates financial or regulatory context for the engagement, but the wording can also describe general advisory work.

occupational_task: Examine and evaluate financial and information systems, recommending controls to ensure system reliability and data integrity.
basis: Evaluating systems and recommending reliability and data-integrity controls is an information-systems or controls-assurance variant, not ownership of system implementation.

occupational_task: Review accounts for discrepancies and reconcile differences.
basis: Reconciliation resolves discrepancies so account balances can be maintained accurately; the audit-related DWA makes assurance use plausible as well.

occupational_task: Report to management regarding the finances of establishment.
basis: Reporting establishment finances to management makes financial information usable for internal decisions; generic financial-statement issuance would instead fall under ACC-01.

occupational_task: Examine whether the organization's objectives are reflected in its management activities, and whether employees understand the objectives.
basis: Testing whether management activity and employee understanding align with organizational objectives is an operational or performance-audit variant, although its DWA also resembles organizational consulting.

occupational_task: Audit payroll and personnel records to determine unemployment insurance premiums, workers' compensation coverage, liabilities, and compliance with tax laws.
basis: The explicit audit of payroll and personnel records produces an assurance and compliance determination; tax and insurance subject matter do not change that responsibility.

occupational_task: Review taxpayer accounts, and conduct audits on-site, by correspondence, or by summoning taxpayer to office.
basis: Authority-side examination of taxpayer accounts is assigned to audit and assurance because the stated occupational outcome is an audit finding; tax subject matter remains a structured secondary link to ACC-04.

occupational_task: Advise clients in areas such as compensation, employee health care benefits, the design of accounting or data processing systems, or long-range tax or estate plans.
basis: The statement's common outcome is client advice for long-range organizational or financial choices, but it combines compensation, benefits, systems, tax, and estate domains that cannot be split under one-to-one mapping.

occupational_task: Review data about material assets, net worth, liabilities, capital stock, surplus, income, or expenditures.
basis: Reviewing assets, liabilities, equity, income, and expenditure data supports accurate period-end records and statements, but the same data can also support management analysis.

occupational_task: Develop treatment plans for radiology patients.
basis: Developing treatment plans is distinct from routine image-based diagnosis and most naturally supports interventional or procedural radiologic care, but the generic wording can also include therapeutic nuclear medicine.

occupational_task: Document the performance, interpretation, or outcomes of all procedures performed.
basis: Documenting the performance and outcome of procedures is integral to procedural care, but 'all procedures performed' can encompass non-interventional and nuclear medicine procedures as well.

occupational_task: Provide counseling to radiologic patients to explain the processes, risks, benefits, or alternative treatments.
basis: Explaining process, risks, benefits, alternatives, and treatments is most characteristic of informed procedural care, but the generic wording can include diagnostic or nuclear medicine encounters.

occupational_task: Assemble and fasten materials to make frameworks or props, using hand tools and wood screws, nails, dowel pins, or glue.
basis: Frameworks can be permanent, but the explicit inclusion of props and the matching O*NET DWA for temporary structures make site-support work the best dominant fit.

occupational_task: Install rough door and window frames, subflooring, fixtures, or temporary supports in structures undergoing construction or repair.
basis: Most listed outputs are permanent rough components; temporary supports create a secondary overlap with the site-support bundle.

occupational_task: Perform minor plumbing, welding, or concrete mixing work.
basis: Minor concrete mixing can directly support forms and posts, while plumbing and welding are adjacent-trade interfaces; no separate bundle is justified by one heterogeneous supplemental statement.

occupational_task: Dig or direct digging of post holes and set poles to support structures.
basis: Setting poles can create a permanent structure, but excavation, support positioning, and direction of site labor align most closely with site-support and foundation-interface work.

occupational_task: Use drones for site surveying and to inspect hard-to-reach areas of a structure.
basis: Drone-based surveying primarily produces site and structure information used to plan and coordinate field work. The same statement also covers inspection of existing structures, creating a real boundary overlap with CAN-47-2031-02; it remains in planning because the wording is not limited to defect-led restoration.
